function.description: Get details for one network bug by bug ID. Use this tool for CSC-style network bug IDs such as CSCwd12345 or CSCwr77118 when the user asks for general bug details, affected versions, severity, workaround, integrated releases, or whether the bug has a workaround across the network. Use this tool only when the user does not specify a particular device, device name, management IP, MAC address, serial number, or networkDeviceId. If the user asks about a bug on a specific device, such as 'details of CSCwd12345 on 50.30.1.9' or 'is device X affected by CSCwd12345', first call get_device_details to resolve the device UUID, then call api_getNetworkBugDeviceForTheBugByNetworkDeviceId with the bug id and resolved networkDeviceId. A CSC ID in a question about bugs is a network bug ID, not a security advisory ID.
function.name: api_getNetworkBugById

id.description: Network bug ID, usually a CSC identifier such as CSCwd12345.

affectedVersions.description: Versions that are affected by the network bug

deviceCount.description: Number of devices which are vulnerable to this network bug

hasWorkaround.description: Indicates if the network bug has a workaround

integratedReleases.description: Versions that have the fix for the network bug

publicationUrl.description: Url for getting network bug details on cisco website

severity.description: 'CATASTROPHIC' - Reasonably common circumstances cause the entire system to fail, or a major subsystem to stop working. 'SEVERE' - Important functions are unusable. 'MODERATE' - Failures occur in unusual circumstances, or minor features do not work at all.

workaround.description: Workaround if any that exists for the network bug
